verdicts.trueWording: more humour in this book than perhaps some previous ones
verdicts.note: Wertzone live fetch 200 (browser UA). Byline 'Adam Whitehead', dated Sunday 29 June 2025, post title 'Written on the Dark by Guy Gavriel Kay'. Quote byte-exact in the paragraph beginning 'The traditional strengths of Kay'. Source hedges with 'perhaps', which the claim drops; substance unchanged.

verdicts.trueWording: quick flash-forward removes the 'will they survive' suspense
verdicts.note: fantasyliterature.com returned 403 to both bare and www live fetches; reached via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20250803031327id_/... (route 2), not a summarizer. Full sentence: '...take the focus away from the usual suspense element of "will they survive" via a quick flash-forward (or an earlier one) so that the reader knows immediately, or already, that the character will do just that — survive.' Paragraph beginning 'But Kay more often than not' confirmed. Byline 'Posted by Bill Capossere', April 18th, 2022.

verdicts.trueWording: plot evokes not 'what happens next' but 'who are they now'
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Verbatim: 'the plot evokes not so much the more traditional "what happens next" response but a "who are they now" response.' Same paragraph as 316; both limbs (the evoked response and the contrast with what-happens-next) present.

verdicts.trueWording: narrator's meta-fictional aside: 'Some tales are told, most are not'
verdicts.note: Verbatim on page: 'As our narrator says in one of the several meta-fictional asides, "Some tales are told, most are not"'. Every limb — narrator, meta-fictional aside, the words themselves — is on the page, in the paragraph beginning 'In a somewhat similar vein'.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay gives us more of those untold tales than most authors
verdicts.note: Clause immediately following the 318 quote in the same sentence: '...and that holds true here as well, but Kay gives us more of those untold tales than most authors.' Byte-exact.

verdicts.trueWording: Danio's elegiac older voice layers an aching sense of time's passage
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'Guidanio ("Danio") Cerra... though his softly elegiac older voice, as he recalls events from a later date layers over the book's present moments an aching sense of time's passage.' Paragraph beginning 'I could go on rapturously' confirmed; the recalling-from-later limb and the layering limb are both explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: novel opens with 'The memory of home can be too far away'
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'The novel opens with the line "The memory of home can be too far away," introducing the twinned ideas of home and exile.' The reviewer does state it is the opening line, so the 'opens with' limb is Capossere's own report, not an inference. Paragraph beginning 'Beyond character and plot' confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: a favourite 'Kay-ism': a few lines of gentle dignity at death
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'Even when death strikes, it's leavened with what has become one of my favorite "Kay-isms" — the lingering of a spirit for a brief while in a few moments consideration of a life lived and now ended, a few lines of gentle dignity, of respect accorded by the author... granted to a wide range of characters'. Kay-ism limb, death-moment limb and granted-to-a-character limb all present. Paragraph beginning 'But Kay also is quick to show' confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay drops into the text so many seeds to prepare us
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'The way Kay drops into the text so many seeds to carefully prepare us for what's to come.' Paragraph beginning 'Finally, the craft is' confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: Repeatedly characters or narrator reflect 'You could die so easily'
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'Repeatedly characters (or the narrator) reflect on how "You could die so easily" or "Death could be so swift."' The claim's 'how easily one could die' is exactly the quoted reflection. Paragraph beginning 'The world Kay creates' confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: characters richly drawn whether central or given two or three paragraphs
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'the characters... are richly drawn and utterly compelling across the board, whether they take up the bulk of the pages, as with Rafel and Lenia, several strands of a few pages each... or are given just two or three paragraphs.' The 'still richly drawn' limb is carried by 'across the board'. Paragraph beginning 'What I'm trying to say here' confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: meticulously crafted in structure, pace, language, dialogue
verdicts.note: Verbatim: 'The novel is meticulously crafted in structure, pace, language, dialogue.' Located in the review's last substantive paragraph, immediately before the publisher's jacket blurb — the cited page location holds.

verdicts.trueWording: 'I found it on the whole to be telling rather than showing'
verdicts.note: Comment thread on the same page, preserved in the Wayback capture. Commenter 'Ilana', April 19, 2022 at 7:30 pm, about Tigana: 'I didn't enjoy it – I found the female characters to be flat and underdeveloped... and I found it on the whole to be telling rather than showing.' Author, date and referent (Tigana, named in the same comment: 'I really didn't like Tigana') all confirmed. The claim's pronoun 'she' is inferred from the name and never stated on the page — incidental, not a substantive limb.

verdicts.trueWording: more explicit storytelling tone than I've come to expect
verdicts.note: strangecurrencies.org live fetch 200. Byline 'Dan Ruffolo June 7, 2022'. First body paragraph, verbatim: 'Taking in places a more explicit storytelling tone than I've come to expect from Guy's work, All the Seas of the World nevertheless captures his scintillating prose...'. The 'in places' limb and the 'from Kay' limb ('from Guy's work') are both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: we can know through the narration of the impacts they had
verdicts.note: Verbatim: '...people who feel much as we do can know, or we can know through the narration, of the impacts they had, the lives they touched, is a salve against that feeling of helplessness.' Both limbs (impacts had, lives touched) present. Paragraph beginning 'This theme feels especially important' confirmed.
